churn_resistance.rationale: Excellent layering: data access, view models and the server boundary each live in one module, and the generated route tree plus a single vite config mean a framework bump touches few files. The main aging risk is the any-typed data layer — API shape changes would surface at runtime, not at compile time.

findings.issue: In-flight fetch promises are cached with no timeout and no AbortController; a hung upstream request leaves a never-settling promise in the cache for the process lifetime, permanently poisoning that resource.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) to fetch (keeping the existing catch-to-evict) so failures eventually clear the cache entry.

findings.issue: The entire PokeAPI layer is typed any (apiGet returns Promise<any>, records cast as any throughout), so response-shape changes surface as runtime bugs with no compile-time signal.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the response shapes actually consumed (species, pokemon, type, move, ability, generation, version-group) and return those from apiGet; the typed view models already prove the shapes are stable.

findings.issue: The 404 page sets its document title by rendering an inline <title> inside <main> and relying on React 19 metadata hoisting, rather than the framework's head() option used by every other route.
findings.suggestion: Serve the not-found page from a splat route (routes/$.tsx) with its own head(), or add a head() override, so title management stays in one mechanism.

findings.issue: Server-only modules are named api.ts/data.ts/server.ts rather than the .server.ts convention; exclusion from the client bundle currently depends on tree-shaking through stripped server-fn handlers.
findings.suggestion: Rename to api.server.ts / data.server.ts (Start's documented convention) so client exclusion is guaranteed by the compiler, not import-graph luck.

findings.issue: Defensive 'as CatalogEntry[]' cast on loader data instead of relying on the inferred server-fn return type.
findings.suggestion: Delete the cast and fix the inference gap (e.g. annotate buildHomeData's return type) — casts at boundaries silently hide type drift.

findings.issue: loaderDeps: () => ({}) is a no-op that adds noise and implies a dependency contract that doesn't exist.
findings.suggestion: Remove the loaderDeps key entirely on this route.

findings.issue: EM_DASH is exported but never imported; em-dash fallbacks are inlined as string literals at call sites instead.
findings.suggestion: Delete the dead export or use it in the '?? "—"' fallbacks.

findings.issue: Unbounded in-memory Map cache with no size cap or TTL.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for this fixed snapshot, but note the assumption in a comment or add a simple cap so the pattern isn't copied verbatim onto a larger, live API.

summary: An unusually current codebase: it pins the exact 1.0-stable TanStack Start release and consistently uses its post-RC APIs (validator(), nitro/vite, Vite 8, shellComponent, head/meta titles), with a lean four-dependency runtime and clean one-module-per-concern layering that keeps framework churn contained. The main aging risks are the any-typed PokeAPI layer, an in-flight-promise cache with no abort/timeout, and a few clever-but-non-idiomatic touches (inline <title>, a defensive cast). Strong PR overall; approve after the fetch-timeout and typing items are addressed.

apis.replacement: Prefer route head() / a splat not-found route for framework-managed titles
